The widths of the confidence intervals reflect increasing uncertainty as the forecast horizon extends further into the future. For the 1-day horizon, uncertainty is minimal because near-term outcomes are more predictable, given the limited room for significant changes or surprises. By the 1-week range, more variability is possible due to external drivers like market movements or news developments, which widens the confidence interval. At the 1-month horizon, uncertainties grow even further because of the cumulative effects of unknown future events or trends, as well as the compounding uncertainty of earlier assumptions. This widening reflects the natural difficulty in precisely forecasting over longer timeframes.

Certain risks and events could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. Additionally, structural shifts, like changes in policy or the emergence of unforeseen risks in the broader environment, could disrupt my assumptions about stability over time and skew outcomes far outside my projected confidence intervals.
